clue.text: Getting a cent in change is not new!

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of a cent in

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gleefully remarks that receiving a cent in change is a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like coins handed back, but it is the anagram signal on A CENT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient is very old, the opposite of fresh or recent.

clue.text: He is aggressive when worker gets hold of a yacht

indicators.note: gets hold of links the worker to the yacht piece that sits beside it

parts.note: as can mean when
a sail can stand for a sailing boat
the ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer turns hostile on acquiring a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: AS (when) is followed by SAIL (a yacht) and ANT (worker).
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, someone who behaves with hostility.

clue.text: Man keeping his head on horseback?

definitions.text: Man keeping his head on horseback?

parts.words: Man keeping his head on horseback?
parts.note: seems to describe a calm rider, but means a creature with a human head and torso on a horse's body

explanation.surface: A rider who stays composed in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a centaur is half human, half horse.

clue.text: Being ahead of time can cause rows among listeners

indicators.note: among places the word for rows inside the word for listeners

parts.note: ears are listeners
lines are rows

explanation.surface: Arriving early may provoke quarrels in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests quarrels, but here it means lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliness is the state of coming before the expected time.

clue.text: Use a ribbon as a model?

definitions.meaning: to work a typewriter, whose inked ribbon prints the letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether a ribbon could serve as a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing uses a typewriter ribbon; a type is also an exemplar or kind.

clue.text: Under German doctor at first, but he's got up

indicators.note: at first places the doctor's letters at the front, ahead of the German word

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
unter is the German word for under

explanation.surface: Someone serves beneath a German physician but has nonetheless risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under German' is not about rank: it asks for the German word for under, UNTER. 'at first' puts MO before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounter is one who climbs up, as onto a horse, so he has got up.

clue.text: They step on a great many feet

definitions.text: They step on a great many feet

parts.words: They step on a great many feet
parts.note: seems to mean clumsy people treading on toes, but describes creatures walking on very many legs

explanation.surface: People who keep treading on others' toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Millipedes are arthropods with a great many pairs of legs.

clue.text: Some of the Mounties may get release

indicators.note: some of signals that the answer is a run of letters inside the word Mounties

explanation.surface: Some Canadian police officers may be let go.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mounties are Canada's mounted police.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to loosen knots, setting something free.

clue.text: Newspaper offers ticket to new lido

parts.note: tab is a ticket or label

indicators.note: new signals the letters of lido are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A paper gives away passes to a newly opened open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIDO is a public open-air swimming pool in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular, compact-format newspaper.

clue.text: This bird can be seen about late in the day

parts.note: re means about or concerning
eve is the evening, late in the day

explanation.surface: A bird spotted flying around at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: The Spaniard one's backing, right?

indicators.note: backing means the letters of one's are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the letters of one's, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A query about whether a Spanish man is supporting someone, correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Senor is the Spanish title for a man, so a Spanish gentleman.

clue.text: It's nice giving a friend a piece of furniture

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: It is pleasant to give a mate an item of furniture as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Palatable means agreeable to the taste, pleasant or acceptable.

clue.text: Applying to characters with a leaning to the right

definitions.text: Applying to characters with a leaning to the right

parts.words: Applying to characters with a leaning to the right
parts.note: seems to describe people of right-wing politics, but means printed letters that slope rightwards

explanation.surface: A description of people whose politics lean to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type is a sloping typeface whose letters slant to the right.

clue.text: Old-fashioned dress few find boring

parts.note: tire is an archaic word for attire or dress
some means a few

explanation.surface: Not many people enjoy dated clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRE is the old word for attire, as in a woman's tire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is tedious, wearying and dull.

clue.text: Domestic flights

parts.note: seems to mean air travel within a country, but means sets of steps inside a home

explanation.surface: Air travel within one country.
explanation.definitionFit: Staircases are flights of stairs, found inside houses.

clue.text: May be eager to correspond

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters of eager could form a different word

explanation.surface: Someone might well be keen to exchange letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to match or be in accord, one sense of correspond.

clue.text: The serving men, the staff one brought over, for a month in France

parts.note: taken as written
RM is the Royal Marines, men serving in the forces

indicators.note: brought over signals that staff and one are turned around as a unit

parts.note: a rod is a staff
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Soldiers, their staff and a recruit are posted abroad for a month in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' reverses ROD I to give IDOR. RM, the Royal Marines, are British seaborne troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermidor was the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, in high summer.

clue.text: The grandee coming if a substitute's needed

indicators.note: substitute's needed asks for the letters of coming if a to be swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman arriving in case a replacement is required.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifico is a Venetian nobleman, hence any grandee or person of high rank.

clue.text: The salesman allowed no-one to be upset, giving satisfaction

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
let means allowed

indicators.note: to be upset means the letters for no-one are turned over in this down clue

parts.note: no and one give NO and the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A salesman refuses to let anyone get annoyed, so all are contented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests annoyance, but in a down entry it turns NOI over to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Repletion is fullness, the state of being satisfied after eating.

clue.text: A roundabout way to gain admission

definitions.text: A roundabout way to gain admission

parts.words: A roundabout way to gain admission
parts.note: seems to mean a devious approach, but is literally a rotating gate through which people enter

explanation.surface: A description of an indirect route into somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving barrier admitting one person at a time.

clue.text: Beasts taking sound exercise on river, river, river

indicators.note: sound signals that the letters entered only have the pronunciation of the rowing word

parts.note: to row is to exercise on a river
the Dee is a river in Britain
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Animals getting healthy exercise by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective for healthy exercise; it marks ROW as said aloud, giving ROE. The Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are small Eurasian deer, wild animals.

clue.text: Get hold of a note to file

parts.note: G is a musical note
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: An instruction to obtain a memo for the filing cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize or clutch firmly.

clue.text: Flat in a French street turned up for dilettante

indicators.note: in puts the flat word inside a plus the reversed street
turned up means the French street is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: rue is French for street
mat is a variant spelling of matt, meaning flat or dull in finish

explanation.surface: An apartment in a Paris street appears for a hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but it is MAT, a dull finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur dabbles in a pursuit without professional skill, as a dilettante does.

clue.text: "The endearing — of female friendship" (Johnson)

parts.note: a quotation from Samuel Johnson with a word missing between endearing and of, which the solver supplies

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Samuel Johnson's Rasselas.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash for the gap: Johnson wrote of the endearing elegance of female friendship in Rasselas.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Johnson's phrase describes graceful refinement, the quality that makes the friendship endearing.

clue.text: Register possibly ten letters to the queen

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of ten might be arranged differently

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten letters should be sent to the monarch to be recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to record or put down in a list or ledger.

clue.text: Sharp undercurrent to get free from

parts.note: read as under current: AC, alternating current, with the next piece under it
to rid is to get free from

explanation.surface: A strong hidden current is hard to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'undercurrent' as 'under current': in a down entry RID sits under AC, alternating current.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means pungent and biting, harsh to taste or smell.

clue.text: Silver seen in the mud? It's just an illusion

indicators.note: seen in places the silver symbol inside the word for mud

parts.note: mire is mud or bog
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Something shiny glimpsed in the mud turns out not to be there.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert.

clue.text: Flag in all the colours of the rainbow!

definitions.meaning: a flag is a wild ..., the yellow flag

definitions.text: all the colours of the rainbow
definitions.meaning: The Greek goddess of the rainbow; the flower is named for its many colours

explanation.surface: A banner showing every colour of the rainbow.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, and Iris personified the rainbow in Greek myth.

clue.text: Speculator responsible for the upturn in gold

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the word for upturn inside the heraldic gold

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a rise is an upturn

explanation.surface: An investor is credited with a rise in the gold price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speculator' suggests a market gambler, but it is someone who forms theories.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser speculates, framing hypotheses about how things work.

clue.text: Old people get very cold before turning in

indicators.note: before places the very cold word ahead of the reversed piece

parts.note: ice is very cold

indicators.note: turning means the little word in is written backwards

explanation.surface: Elderly folk feel chilly before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' sounds like pensioners, but means an ancient tribe: the Iceni of Boudicca in eastern Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca against Rome.

clue.text: Note brightly coloured and very large screen

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
red is a bright colour
OS is outsize, a clothing size meaning very large

explanation.surface: A memo about a big vivid display screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: This is below the belt, in front of a Scotsman

definitions.text: This is below the belt, in front of a Scotsman

parts.words: This is below the belt, in front of a Scotsman
parts.note: seems to hint at a foul blow, but describes the pouch hung from the belt over a kilt

explanation.surface: A hint at an unfair punch aimed at a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a low blow in boxing; the object is the pouch worn at the front of a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the fur or leather pouch worn hanging at the front of Highland dress.
